=== changelog.d/mm-472.added.md
A blob GC pass that skipped accounts now reports it: the new `blob_gc_errors_total` metric and an `errors` field on each sweep in `GET /v1/admin/health` distinguish a pass that ran but left work undone from one that is not completing at all (which still shows as a stale timestamp).
=== changelog.d/mm-472.fixed.md
Blob garbage collection no longer deletes the blobs of an account whose repo walk failed. Previously, when reconciling an account errored, that account's blobs were never pinned permanent and the sweep collected them once their upload grace expired — destroying the ownership row, the stored blob, and the file, and then propagating those deletions to the mirror bucket. The sweep now excludes any account that failed to reconcile in the same pass, so blobs whose references could not be computed are never collected; such an account retains its blobs until the underlying fault is fixed.
=== changelog.d/mm-473.fixed.md
Listing the records of a collection no longer fails, or risks returning another collection's records, when the repository holds record keys shorter than the requested collection name. The underlying repository library's prefix scan yields such keys even though they fall outside the requested range; every key is now re-checked against the collection prefix and the scan stops as soon as it passes the end of that range, which also makes listing a small collection cheaper. Because the leak previously surfaced as an error, listing a collection could fail permanently for an affected account and, in turn, block blob reconciliation for it.

content.text:
`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- `set-version` is the single mutation point for a release: it bumps `[workspace.package]` (all crates share one version), rolls the `changelog.d/*.{type}.md` fragments into `CHANGELOG.md` under the new heading, and **restamps the generated operator reference docs** — that last part exists because `docs-check` compares those pages against a version stamp, so a bump without it would fail CI.
- Note there is deliberately no `Unreleased` section: the fragment directory *is* the unreleased state, which is what lets the `changelog-check` gate demand a fragment per PR.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Committing and opening the version-bump PR.

content.text:
The merge was blocked by the permission classifier — merging a PR is an outward-facing action it wants you to sign off on.

**Status so far:** [PR #440 "Release 0.8.4"](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/440) is open with every check green (PDS gate, both iOS compile lanes, CodeQL, CodeRabbit). It contains only the `just set-version 0.8.4` output — version bump, changelog roll-up of MM-472/MM-473, operator reference restamp.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- Merging is the point of no return for *staging*, not production: Railway watches `main` with "Wait for CI", so the squash-merge itself triggers the staging deploy. Production only moves when the `production` branch is advanced to the tag.
- That's why the release is a three-step ratchet — merge (staging), `just release` (cuts `v0.8.4`), `just deploy-production v0.8.4` (promotes). The `verify-release` job on `production` refuses any tip whose tag doesn't match the workspace version, so a mismatched promotion can't deploy.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`

Please merge it (squash) — either from the GitHub UI or:

```bash
gh pr merge 440 --squash --delete-branch
```

Once it's merged, tell me and I'll run `just release` to cut the `v0.8.4` tag and then `just deploy-production v0.8.4` to promote — I'll check with you again before that promotion step.

One thing worth flagging for after this ships: production still carries the manual `temp_until = NULL` blob pin from the 2026-07-25 loss incident. MM-472 and MM-473 are exactly the fixes that pin was waiting on, so once 0.8.4 is live and a clean GC sweep reports `errors: 0`, that pin should be revisited.
